6.  APPEAL OF THE DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DECISION TO DENY AN EXTENSION
  OF TEMPORARY USE PERMIT NO. 2020-01 FOR TRUCK-TRAILER STORAGE AT 8530 ALAMEDA
  STREET

  Senior Planner Yalini Siva presented a staff report to the Planning Commission. This staff report
  included a background on previous company, change in company, original issuance of Temporary
  Use Permit (“TUP”), definition of TUP, and recommendation that the Planning Commission uphold
  the Community Development Director’s decision to deny an extension of the Temporary Use
  Permit No. 2020-01, based on the South Gate Municipal Code (“SGMC”).

  City Attorney Craig Hardwick referred to the SGMC Section 11.21.020 which notes that "Any land
  use that is not specifically listed in the land use tables for the applicable zone shall not be allowed
  or permitted within the zone." This request will not be granted even if the commissioners chose

Minutes  Page 1 of 4
Planning Commission Meeting  4
   ITEM NO. 1

  to approve the request. This hearing was held, out of abundance of consideration to allow due
  process, to give the applicant an opportunity to plead their case before the Planning Commission
  as stipulated in the SGMC.

  Director Meredith Elguira informed the Planning Commission that there was a change in operation
  and in the company back in 2020, and the TUP was issued to Alameda Engle & Properties in error.

  Attorney Alfred Frajio Jr. (304 S Broadway Suite 350, Los Angeles Ca 90013- SOMOS Law Grou),
  represents Alameda Engle & Properties. Mr. Frajio requested an adequate extension to meet with
  City officials and come to an agreement regarding an extension of the Temporary Use Permit. He
  claimed the TUP was issued for one year with an option to extend it for five (5) additional years
  and it was issued by former staff members. He also addressed the following: the authority to
  remedy the previous administration’s errant requirements for a TUP, legal non-conforming use
  that has not been abandoned or discontinued, the right to continue the use is protected and
  preserved pursuant to the SGMC, active Fleet Yard business license, and compliance with the TUP
  conditions.

  Property Owner Alan Engle (8530 S. Alameda Street South Gate Alameda Engle & Company) gave
  a brief explanation of the services his company provides and when Fleet Yard Inc. was established
  at the property located at 8530 S. Alameda Street. He indicated that Fleet Yard Inc. replaced
  Alameda Engle & Company in 2020.

  Business Owner Daniel Otting (Fleet Yard Inc., 8440 S Alameda St Los Angeles Ca) gave a brief
  overview of his company and services provided to the community.

  Public Speaker Jenifer Ganata (6325 Pacific Blvd Ste 300, Huntington Park, CA 90255) asked if Engle
  is using the site or are they leasing it?

  Attorney Frajio stated that Fleet Yard Inc. is currently leasing the property.

  Director Elguira informed the commissioners that the property is zoned IF. The zone changed from
  M3 to Industrial Flex (IF) in 2015. She stated it is unclear why this TUP was issued by the former
  administration and provided examples of TUP allowed events.

  Chair Delgado asked about grandfather status of the project.

  City Attorney Hardwick explained that there is a factual difference between the City and the
  Appellant’s claims regarding grandfather and legal non-conforming use.

  Commissioner Prieto requested an explanation on number of days and consecutive days.

  Director Elguira explained the period of time allowed under the TUP and why the permit should
  never have been issued based on time and use.

  Commissioner Prieto asked what type of use was approved under the current permit.

Minutes  Page 2 of 4

  Director Elguira stated that the current permit was issued on the new use which is the truck
  container storage. She stated that the truck storage use never legally existed.

  Commissioner Ozaeta asked if the TUP is under the discretion of the City.

  Director Elguira stated that the TUP must comply with the code.

  Commissioner Laborin acknowledged that the TUP was issued by mistake however there must be
  away to allow the use being requested.

  Director Elguira explained that the code does not allow prohibited uses from continuing to
  operate. She reiterated that the Planning Commission’s decision is limited to the appeal of the
  Director’s decision to deny the TUP extension request.

  MOTION: Chairperson Delgado moved to accept the determination that this matter is exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act; adopt the findings as outlined in Resolution No.
  2023-02 (Attachment A); and uphold the decision of the Director of Community Development
  denying an extension of TUP No. 2020- 01 by adopting Resolution No. 2023-05., and Commissioner

SUBJECT: CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 865 TO PERMIT THE SALE OF BEER, WINE, AND
DISTILLED SPIRITS IN CONJUNCTION WITH A FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT FOR ON-SITE
CONSUMPTION (TYPE 47 ABC LICENSE) AT 13610 GARFIELD AVENUE.

PURPOSE: To consider Conditional Use Permit No. 865 to permit the sale of beer, wine and distilled spirits for
on-site consumption, in conjunction with a bona-fide eating establishment, located at 13610 Garfield Avenue.

RECOMMENDED ACTION:
1. CONDUCT a public hearing, pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Table 11.51-1 and Section
  11.50.040.B;
2. ACCEPT the determination that this matter is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act; and
3. ADOPT the findings as outlined in Resolution No. 2023-06 (Attachment A).

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: Advertising and notification of the public hearing for the application was
conducted in compliance with Chapter 11.50, of the South Gate Municipal Code. Notice of the hearing was
originally posted and published in the “South Gate Press” newspaper and was mailed to surrounding properties
on May 4, 2023.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: The City of Southgate has determined that the proposed Conditional
Use Permit is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) as a Class 1
Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15303 of the CEQA Guidelines. Class 1 consists of the operation,
repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures,
facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use beyond
that existing at the time of the lead agency's determination.

BACKGROUND: The subject parcel is located at 13610 Garfield Avenue and sits on the southeast corner
Garfield Avenue and Century Boulevard (Assessor’s Parcel Number 6242-001-001). The parcel measures roughly
261 feet by 121 feet (31,581 square feet). Access is granted on to the parcel via driveways from northbound
Garfield Avenue and from eastbound Century Boulevard. Seventeen off -street parking spaces service the project
site, 16 standard spaces and 1 accessible space.

  8
 The property is zoned HMU-1 and is located within the Hollydale Specific Plan Area. In the heart of the City’s
Garfield Corridor, the subject parcel helps to make up an important portion of the City of South Gate’s geography.
The Hollydale Specific Plan focuses on the area around the Garfield Avenue and Main Street intersection, which
offers tremendous potential as a lively neighborhood district that is a local community gathering place and
contains a mix of neighborhood serving uses to meet the daily needs of residents. The Hollydale Mixed Use-1
(HMU-1) zone is intended to promote and reinforce pedestrian-oriented retail, restaurant and entertainment uses
in a “main street” setting along Garfield Avenue, while also promoting infill mixed use development. This mixed-
use zone includes a variety of uses in a neighborhood setting scaled for pedestrian visitors and local shoppers.
Upper level residential and/or office uses are encouraged to add “eyes on the street” as well as increase retail
demand. The street environment should be focused on making Garfield Avenue a welcoming place to visit, shop
and stay. This Zone is consistent with the “Main Street” Place type in the General Plan.

ANALYSIS: The applicant, Kevin Hufford (Representative), on behalf of 13610 Garfield, LLC (Applicant), has
submitted a request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to permit the sale of beer wine and distilled spirits in

  9
 conjunction with a bona-fide eating place.

The Applicant is in the process of securing a Type-47 License for the sale of beer, wine and spirits for on-site
consumption from the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC).

The site is zoned HMU-1 (Hollydale Mixed Use) which permits alcohol sales as part of a bona fide eating place
with a Conditional Use Permit.

The proposal to serve beer, wine and spirits shall be limited to the area within the restaurant building. All alcohol
storage shall be maintained in or behind the counter area. Service shall be limited to the interior of the restaurant
building.

The Hollydale Specific Plan permits the requested use via a CUP and in fact encourages uses that promote
economic growth in the community, which has expressed a strong desire for attracting a variety of attractive and
desirable neighborhood-serving retail along Garfield Avenue such as a grocery store, pharmacy, convenience
retail, clothing stores, gymnasiums, hardware stores, nighttime draws such as restaurants and coffee shops, and
other places for residents and visitors to congregate.

While the Specific Plan corridors along Garfield, Paramount and Imperial Highway have experienced trying
economic conditions, the community has expressed strong desire to build on Hollydale’s history, diversity and
intimate scale.

The proposed use will enable the restaurant operator to serve a larger and more varied clientele, thereby creating
a more desirous economic condition in the community.

Conditional Use Permit Findings
The findings for Conditional Use Permit No. 865 are provided below:

1. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of this title or the
  city’s general plan.
  The subject property has a designated zoning of Hollydale Mixed Use-1 (“HMU1”), is located within the
  Hollydale Specific Plan area, and sits on the southeastern corner between Garfield Avenue and Century
  Boulevard. Approval of the CUP and the related business aids in promoting development opportunities for
  international and national retailers while supporting existing local businesses.

2. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the existing and
  future land uses of the applicable zone.
  Per SGMC Section 11.21.030, Table 11.21-4: Commercial Industrial Zones Allowed Land Uses, alcohol
  sales, as part of a restaurant requires a Conditional Use Permit. The project proposal is for the sale of beer,
  wine, and distilled spirits in conjunction with a restaurant.

3. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character or
  function of the neighborhood.
  Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character or
  function of the neighborhood, as the project proposal does not constitute a material change in use or an

  10
   intensification of use in the vicinity of the project site.

4. The project proposal is exempt from CEQA under Class 1 Categorical Exemption.
  The proposed Conditional Use Permit is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) as a under Class 1 Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15303 of the CEQA Guidelines.
  Class 1 consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of
  existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving
  negligible or no expansion of use beyond that existing at the time of the lead agency's determination.

CONCLUSION: Based on the analysis provided above, it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning
Commission approve Conditional Use Permit No. 865. The proposed conditions of approval contained in
Resolution No. 2023-06 require that the business operation remain in compliance with the requirements of the
California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control and are designed to mitigate any potential negative impacts
and address any potential problems that may arise should there be a change in the business operations and/or
management. Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Conditional Use Permit No. 856,
authorizing the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for on-site consumption in connection with a Type 47 ABC
license at a bona fide eating place.

  CUP NO. 865 – CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL:

Violation of, or noncompliance with, any of these conditions shall constitute grounds for
revocation of this permit:
1.  No alcoholic beverages, including beer and wine, shall be sold from the premises for off-sale
  uses.
2.  No alcohol sales displays shall be permitted that are visible from the public street or parking
  lot.
3.  Employees selling alcoholic beverages shall be of an age consistent with Section 25663 of the
  California Business and Professions Code.
4.  The permittee shall comply with all state statutes, rules and regulations relating to the sale,
  purchase, display, possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages.
5.  The premises shall be maintained in a neat and orderly manner at all times.
6.  Building and site design and maintenance shall be consistent with the standards of the
  immediate neighborhood so as not to cause blight or deterioration, or to substantially diminish
  or impair property values within the neighborhood.
7.  The owner/operator or lessee shall be responsible for the conduct of all employees, including
  their education concerning Alcoholic Beverage Control regulations and provisions of the
  South Gate Municipal Code pertaining to sales of alcohol (e.g., verification of age of
  purchaser).
8.  The permittee shall acknowledge that the city has specifically reserved the right and authority
  to impose sanctions, including suspension or revocation of the CUP, as a consequence of one
  or more violations of a state statute, rule, or regulation concerning the sale to or consumption
  of alcoholic beverages by a minor.
9.  The permit shall be subject to compliance review of the property and CUP conditions at
  planning-commission-established intervals; the first compliance review shall occur within six
  months of permit issuance or actuation.
10. The permit shall, after notice to the permittee and an opportunity to be heard, be subject to
  additional conditions to maintain or remedy land use compatibility, security, or crime control
  issues that have arisen since the issuance of the permit.
11. Conditional Use Permit No. 865 is an approval for the sale of alcohol in conjunction with
  prepared meals. This approval is based on the floor plan submitted for the proposed project.
  Violation of any of the conditions of approval shall be cause for revocation of the Conditional
  Use Permit.
12. Within thirty (30) days after issuance of the permit, the permittee shall certify his/her
  acceptance of the conditions placed on the approval by signing a notarized Affidavit of
  Acceptance stating that he/she accepts and shall be bound by all of the conditions.
13. The permittee shall defend, hold harmless and indemnify the City and its agents, officers and
  employees from any claim, action or proceeding against the City or its agents, officers or
  employees to attack, set aside, void or annul any approval by the City concerning the project.
  The City shall promptly notify the permittee of any filed claim, action or proceeding and shall
  cooperate fully in the defense of the action.

  14
 14. The permittee shall acknowledge and agree that the City has a legitimate and compelling
  governmental interest in the permittee’s strict compliance with all conditions imposed upon
  the permit, including adherence to state status, rules and regulations as specified in this
  section. The permittee shall further acknowledge and agree that any violation of a state statue,
  rule or regulation concerning the sale to or consumption of alcoholic beverages by a minor
  has been determine by the city to have a deleterious secondary effect upon (i) the specific land
  use requested by the permittee and authorized by the city; (ii) the compatibility or permittee’s
  authorized land use with adjacent land uses; and (iii) the welfare and safety of the general
  public within the city. In view of such deleterious secondary effects, permittee shall
  acknowledge that the city has specifically reserved the right and authority to impose sanctions,
  including suspension or revocation of the conditional use permit, as a consequence of one or
  more violations of a state statue, rule or regulation concerning the sale to or consumption of
  alcoholic beverages by a minor.
15. Any violation by permittee of any condition of this permit, or of any ordinance or statute
  concerning sale of alcoholic beverages to a minor or otherwise may result in the suspension
  or revocation of the permit at the discretion of the Planning Commission. The permit may be
  revoked and reissued with new or modified conditions, as may be appropriate under the
  circumstances.

16. Reimbursement to the City for all costs and expenses reasonably incurred in investigating,
  identifying, and documenting the violation, and in processing information concerning the
  violation, may be imposed as a condition of the continuation, reinstatement, or reissuance of
  any permit.

17. For the duration of any suspension of an alcohol-related CUP, the Planning Commission, or,
  upon any appeal, the City Council, may direct the permittee to post a sign on the premises of
  the establishment relating to such suspension. The size, content, and location of such sign
  shall be as specified by the Director of Community Development.

18. A public hearing consistent with Chapter 11.50 (Administration) shall be held for the
  consideration of a permit revocation. A permit or any associated conditions may be revoked
  or modified by the Planning Commission subject to any of the following grounds:

  a.  The permit or approval was obtained by fraud.
  b.  The property is not being used for the purpose which is the subject of the permit.
  c.  The use for which the approval was granted has ceased or has been suspended for one
  (1) year or more.
  d.  The permit or conditions of the approval have been violated; exercised contrary to the
  terms of approval; or in violation of any statute, ordinance, law or regulation.
  e.  The use for which the approval was granted was exercised in a manner detrimental to the
  public health or safety, or as to constitute a public nuisance.

19. Any approval or permit granted by the City becomes null and void if the property is not being
  used for the approved or permitted purpose within one year from the date the approval or
  permits was issued, consistent with the provisions identified within Section 11.55
  Nonconforming Uses and Buildings.

20. If the application or any conditions of the CUP violate the Zoning Code or do not fulfill the
  intent of the Code, the Planning Commission shall, following a public hearing, be authorized
  to take the following actions:
  15
   a.  Revoke the CUP, revoke and reissue the CUP with new or modified conditions, or modify
  the conditions of the existing CUP as may be appropriate under the circumstances.
  b.  Impose, as a condition of the continuation, reinstatement, or reissuance of the CUP, a
  requirement that the permittee reimburse the City for all costs and expenses reasonably
  incurred in investigating, identifying, and documenting the violation, and in processing
  information concerning the violation for presentation to the Planning Commission, and,
  upon any appeal, to the City Council.
  c.  A CUP shall be revocable if the exercises of rights granted by the CUP are discontinued
  for six (6) consecutive months. The use subject to the CUP may not be resumed of the
  CUP is revoked; a new CUP, including processing and public notification, shall be
  required.

21. If the conditions of any CUP issued pursuant to this chapter are violated by the permittee, or
  by anyone acting under the authority of the permittee, the Planning Commission shall, in
  accordance with the procedures and noticing requirements set forth in Chapter 11.51, Permits
  and Procedures, be authorized to take the following actions:
  a.  First violation: a 15-day permit suspension.
  b.  Second violation occurring within three (3) years of the first violation: 60-day permit
  suspension.
  c.  Third violation occurring within three (3) years of the second violation: the permit shall
  be revoked.

22. Hours of operation for beer, wine and distilled spirit sales and on-site consumption shall be
  Thursday, Friday and Saturday between 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m.; and 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m.
  Sunday to Wednesday.

23. Minor modifications to these conditions may be requested, reviewed and determined by the

SERVICE RESTAURANT AT 4707 FIRESTONE BOULEVARD.

PURPOSE: To consider Conditional Use Permit No. 866 to permit the sale of beer and wine for on-site
consumption to California Fish Grill (CFG), Inc. (“Applicant”), in conjunction with a bona-fide eating
establishment at 4707 Firestone Blvd, within the Azalea Regional Shopping Center.

RECOMMENDED ACTION:
1. CONDUCT a public hearing, pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Table 11.51-1 and Section
  11.50.040.B;
2. ACCEPT the determination that this matter is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act; and
3. ADOPT the findings as outlined in Resolution No. 2023-07 (Attachment A).

repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures,
facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use beyond

BACKGROUND: The subject site is located within the Azalea Regional Shopping Center and lies at the
southerly portion of the lot. The site will be housed at 4707 Firestone in between suites containing an AT&T store
immediately to the west and Chipotle immediately to the east. CFG will occupy the center unit.

  19
 The Shopping Center parcel measures approximately 34 acres (+/- 1,481,040 SF) and lies at the northwest corner
of Firestone Boulevard and Atlantic Avenue. The parcel is rectangular in shape and relatively flat. Parking is
provided via shared parking spaces oriented at the center of the development. Approximately 300 off-street
parking spaces serve the development. Access to the parcel is achieved via Atlantic Avenue from the northwest
and Firestone Boulevard from the east and south.

  SUBJECT SITE
  4707 FIRESTONE

The proposal to serve beer and wine shall be limited to the area within the restaurant building. All alcohol storage
shall be maintained in or behind the counter area. Service shall be limited to the interior of the restaurant building.

ANALYSIS: The applicant, Terry Womack (Representative), on behalf of Azalea Joint Venture, LLC
(Applicant), has submitted a request for a Conditional Use Permit to permit the sale of beer and wine in

  20
 conjunction with a restaurant (bona-fide eating place). The Applicant is currently securing a Type 41 License for
the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption from the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC).

The applicant has submitted construction documents for a tenant improvement permit to improve the location
with a new grease interceptor, cooking facilities, storage, restrooms and dining area. The construction documents
have been submitted for concurrent review for building permits.

The Shopping Center is zoned RC (Regional Commercial) and restaurants are a permitted use. Alcohol sales
require a Conditional Use Permit. The Land Use designation is Industrial, but the Community Design Element in
the 2035 Southgate General plan has designated the following land uses to be highly desirable:

  •  Urban Village
  •  Single Use Retail
  •  Open Space

The preferred land use type occurring at this location is Urban Village where the intended physical character is
to provide a comfortable, walkable environment for shoppers and diners. The proposed use corresponds with the
goals of the General Plan.

Conditional Use Permit Findings
The findings for Conditional Use Permit No. 865 are provided below:

1. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of this title or the
  city’s general plan.
  The subject property has a designated zoning of Regional Commercia (“RC”) and sits on the Northerly portion
  of Firestone Blvd west of Atlantic Avenue. Approval of the CUP and the related business aids in promoting
  development opportunities for international and national retailers while supporting existing local businesses.

2. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the existing and
  future land uses of the applicable zone.
  Per SGMC Section 11.21.030, Table 11.21-4: Commercial Industrial Zones Allowed Land Uses, alcohol
  sales, as part of a restaurant requires a Conditional Use Permit. The project proposal is for the sale of beer and
  wine in conjunction with a restaurant.

3. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character or
  function of the neighborhood.
  Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character or
  function of the neighborhood, as the project proposal does not constitute any changes in use or an
  intensification of use in the remainder of the Azalea Shopping Center.

4. The project proposal is exempt from CEQA under Class 3 Categorical Exemption.
  The proposed Conditional Use Permit is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) as a under Class 1 Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15303 of the CEQA Guidelines.
  Class 1 consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of

  21
   existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving
  negligible or no expansion of use beyond that existing at the time of the lead agency's determination.
CONCLUSION: Based on the analysis provided above, it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning
Commission approve Conditional Use Permit No. 866. The proposed conditions of approval contained in
Resolution No. 2023-07 require that the business operations remain in compliance with the requirements of the
California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control and are designed to mitigate any potential negative impacts
and address any potential problems that may arise should there be a change in the business operations and/or
management. Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Conditional Use Permit No. 866,
authorizing the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption in connection with a Type 41 ABC license at a bona
fide eating place.
